_comment: SPIKE A fixtures — the reference text for each supported language.
WHY THESE SENTENCES. Each fixture is chosen to exercise the failure mode the
match step exists to catch, not to be easy. Every one contains at least one
token whose SPOKEN form differs from its DISPLAY form — a numeral, an
abbreviation, a symbol, or a year. Those are exactly the places where the
predicted-alignment design broke (spec 6.2) and where the observed->display
match must now prove itself. A fixture of plain prose would pass trivially
`expect_hard` names the display substrings we KNOW will not appear verbatim
in a transcript. If a run reports 100% matched and these were not resolved by
the normalizer path, the harness is measuring the wrong thing.

ROUTING CORRECTED 2026-08-09 (owner): es and fr are FISH AUDIO s2-pro, not Gemini. Gemini entered the routing table only as the Haitian Creole path; ht was removed from scope on 2026-08-08, so Gemini left with it. The first SPIKE A run measured es/fr against Gemini audio -- a provider the product will not ship -- which makes that half of the result an artifact of the wrong input, not a measurement of the design.

VOICE CORRECTED 2026-08-09 (owner): the es fixture was using Jacynthe, an ENGLISH Fish voice, to read Spanish. Fish s2-pro is multilingual so it produced audio, but an English-accented voice reading Spanish is not what ships and is not what should be measured -- it degrades recognition for a reason that has nothing to do with the design. motionmax's Fish roster has no Spanish voice, so this ID comes from Fish's own catalogue, filtered to languages=['es']. fr was already correct (Miriam, French Female).
fr voice set to Mario (French Male, d12dae2d...) 2026-08-09 per owner. Robert (a5d7dcbb...) is the alternate; both are French Male s2-pro from the reference stack's roster.

fr LOCKED to Robert (a5d7dcbb..., French Male) 2026-08-09. Measured against Miriam and Mario on identical text and identical engines: Miriam 88.2%, Mario 94.4%, Robert 100% agreement within 250 ms. VOICE CHOICE IS A WORD-SYNC VARIABLE -- a 12-point swing with nothing else changed. This belongs in the voices catalogue as a per-voice property, not as a footnote in a spike.

HOLDOUT added 2026-08-09: different text, same voices. The per-language calibration offset is FIT on `languages` and SCORED on `holdout`. Fitting and scoring on one clip would choose a parameter that makes the bar pass, which is what the pre-fixed drift bound and language scope exist to prevent -- the discipline has to apply to calibration too or it is theatre.
